Physician  Assistant-  Medical  Case  Challenge                               Event  Category:  Health  Professions
………………………………………………………………………………………………………………
 
Eligible  Divisions:  Secondary  &  Postsecondary/  Collegiate  
Round  One: 50  Q  test  (60  minutes)   Digital  Upload:  NO  
Team  Event:  2  competitors  Round  Two: Patient  Case  Review  (15  minutes)  +  Presentation  (5  minutes)         
  Presentation  Materials:  Notes  from  case  review  prep    
New  for  2026-2027
 This  is  a  new  event  for  2026-2027.    
Event  Summary
 The  Physician  Assistant  (PA)  competitive  event  allows  HOSA  members  to  gain  knowledge  and  assessment  techniques  needed  
for
 
a
 
career
 
in
 
the
 
PA
 
profession.
 
This
 
event
 
consists
 
of
 
two
 
rounds,
 
and
 
each
 
team
 
consists
 
of
 
two
 
people.
 
Round
 
One
 
will
 
consist
 
of
 
a
 
written
 
multiple-choice
 
test,
 
and
 
the
 
score
 
will
 
be
 
used
 
to
 
determine
 
which
 
teams
 
qualify
 
for
 
Round
 
Two.
 
In
 
Round
 
Two
 
teams
 
will
 
review
 
case
 
documentation
 
to
 
determine
 
a
 
diagnosis
 
and
 
develop
 
an
 
appropriate
 
treatment
 
plan
 
for
 
the
 
patient.
  
  
Sponsorship
 
HOSA-Future  Health  Professionals  appreciates  the  sponsorship  of  this  event  by  the  PA  Education  Association.  
  
General  Event  Information
 
General  Rules   Competitors  must  be  familiar  with  and  adhere  to  the  General  Rules  and  Regulations.  
Dress  Code  Proper  business  attire  or  ofﬁcial  HOSA  uniform.  Bonus  points  will  be  awarded  for  proper  dress.  All  team  members  must  be  properly  dressed  to  receive  bonus  points.  
Competitors  Must  Provide  ●  Photo  ID for  both  rounds  ●  #2  lead  pencils  (NOT  mechanical)  with  eraser  for  both  rounds  ●  Neon  colored  foam  earplugs,  NOT  earbuds,  for  noise  control  (Rd1-optional)  ●  Copy  of  textbook  (optional)  HOSA  Conference  Staff  will  provide  equipment  and  supplies  listed  in  Appendix  I.  
Ofﬁcial  References  ●  Papadakis,  Rabow,  McQuaid,  Nadler,  and  Price.   Current  Medical  Diagnosis  &  Treatment  2026.  McGraw  Hill.   Latest  Edition.   ●  MedlinePlus  
   
 Physician  Assistant-  Med  Case  Challenge   ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)      Page  1  of  5  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   

ROUND  ONE-  Test
 
Test  Instructions  All  competitors  will  be  given  a  test  and  answer  sheet.   The  written  test  will  consist  of  50  multiple-choice  items  in  a  maximum  of  60  minutes.  See  test  instructions  here.  The  team  test  score  average  from  Round  One  will  be  used  to  qualify  the  team  for  the  Round  Two  presentation.   
Time  Remaining  Announcements  
There  will  be  NO  verbal  announcements  for  time  remaining  during  ILC  testing.  All  ILC  testing  will  be  completed  in  the  Testing  Center,  and  competitors  are  responsible  for  monitoring  their  own  time.  
Written  Test  Plan  The  written  test  for  Medical  Case  Challenge  is:  ●  Disease  Process  &  Terminology  (includes  cancer  &  neoplasms)-  10%  ●  Body  Systems:  ○  Integumentary  -   4%  ○  Musculoskeletal  -  6%  ○  Circulatory  &  Lymphatic  -  10%  ○  Respiratory  -  6%  ○  Digestive  -  10%  ○  Endocrine  -  6%  ○  Nervous  &  Senses  -  8%  ○  Reproductive  -   4%  ○  Urinary  -   4%  ○  Mental  Disorders  -  6%   ●  Patient  Assessment-  12%  ●  Diagnosis-  14%  
Sample  Test  Questions  1.  Kidneys  contain  millions  of  tiny  structures  called  what?  (https://medlineplus.gov/kidneydiseases.html )  A.  Cysts  B.  Ureters  C.  Nephrons  D.  Calyx   2.  Which  one  of  these  diseases  are  Antibody  Serology  Tests  not  used  to  detect?  (https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/antibody-serology-tests/ )  A.  Hepatitis  B.  Cancer  C.  Osteoperosis  D.  Severe  autoimmune  disorders   3.  A  patient  might  have  a  Uvulopalatopharyngoplasty  (UPPP)  to  treat  what  condition?  (https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/007663.htm )  A.  Impacted  molar  B.  Sleep  apnea  C.  Cavity  D.  Canker  sores   
    
 Physician  Assistant-  Med  Case  Challenge   ILC  Guidelines  (September  2026)      Page  2  of  5  The  expectation  is  that  competitors  read  and  are  aware  of  all  the  content  within  these  guidelines  and  associated  links.  Successful  competitors  will  study  all  links  for  the  detailed  information.   
ROUND  TWO-  The  Case  Review  &  Presentation
 
1.  The  top  teams  from  Round  One  will  advance  to  Round  Two.  The  number  of  advancing  teams  will  be  determined  by  the  scores  obtained  in  Round  One  and  the  space  and  time  available  for  Round  Two.  Round  Two  ﬁnalists  will  be  announced  on-site  at  ILC  per  the  conference  agenda.  
2.  The  team  will  be  supplied  with  supporting  documents  for  a  selected  complex  medical  case.   
3.  The  team  will  be  allowed  to  use  their  textbook  and  all  identiﬁed  resources  during  the  review  of  the  medical  case.   
4.  The  team  will  have  15  minutes  to  evaluate  the  documentation  and  formulate  a  case  prevention.   
5.  The  case  presentation  should  include  the  following:  a.  Patient  information  and  clinical  course;  patient’s  clinical  condition  and  progression  of  the  disease  process  presented  in  chronological  order  b.  Accurate  diagnosis  c.  Treatment  plan;  appropriate  treatment  plan  (including  all  aspects  of  treatment)  
6.  The  team  will  have  ﬁve  (5)  minutes  to  present  their  ﬁndings  to  a  group  of  judges.  Teams  are  allowed  to  use  their  notes  from  the  15  minute  evaluation  in  the  presentation  with  judges.  No  other  materials  are  allowed.   
7.  The  timekeeper  will  announce  when  there  is  one  (1)  minute  remaining  in  the  presentation. The  timekeeper  will  stop  the  presentation  after  ﬁve  (5)  minutes.  
8.  Both  team  members  must  take  an  active  role  in  the  presentation.    
Final  Scoring 1.  The  team  test  score  average  will  be  added  to  the  presentation  score  to  determine  ﬁnal  results.    2.  In  case  of  a  tie,  the  highest  average  test  score  will  determine  the  rank.    
Future  Opportunities  The  HOSA  Scholarship  program  has  funding  available  for  HOSA  members  who  have  an  interest  in  various  health  careers!   The  application  process  begins  January  1,  2027,  and  can  be  found  here: https://hosa.org/scholarships/.   Graduating  from  high  school  or  completing  your  postsecondary/collegiate  program  does  not  mean  your  HOSA  journey  has  to  
end.

All  pertinent  information  is  included. The  information  consists  of  both  objective  and  subjective  data.  Demographics,  chief  complaint,  past  medical  history,  social  and  family  history  are  included.  
Most  of  the  pertinent  information  is  included.   
Some  of  the  pertinent  information  is  included.  
Little  of  the  pertinent  case  information  is  included.  
The  presentation  lacks  pertinent  information.  
 
2.  Patient’s  clinical  course:
 
patient’s
 clinical  condition  and  progression  of  the  disease  process  presented  in  chronological  order.  
The  clinical  course  is  clearly  deﬁned  and  includes  information  regarding  the  patient’s  clinical  condition  and  progression  of  the  disease  process.   The  information  is  presented  in  chronological  order.   
Most  of  the  clinical  course  is  mostly  deﬁned  but  some  clinical  condition  and  progression  is  missing.  
Some  aspects  of  the  clinical  course  are  included,  but  more  information  is  needed  regarding  the  condition  and  course.  
There  is  signiﬁcant  amount  of  information  regarding  the  condition  and  course  is  missing.  
The  clinical  course  is  not  included  in  the  presentation.

4.  Treatment  plan  for  the  patient.

Limited  aspects  of  items  for  an  appropriate  treatment  plan  for  the  patient.  
The  presentation  did  not  include  an  appropriate  treatment  plan  for  the  identiﬁed  patient.  
 
B.  Presentation  Organization
 
EXCELLENT  10  points  
GOOD  8  points  
AVERAGE  6  points  
FAIR  4  points  
POOR  0  points  
JUDGE  SCORE  
1.  The  presentation  organization  
The  presentation  was  concise,  thorough,  and  included  all  key  points.   The  presentation  kept  the  audience’s  attention.  
The  information  shared  was  relevant  and  included  most  key  points.   Very  few  key  points  were  missing.  
The  presentation  was  mostly  thorough,  but  some  key  points  were  not  included.  
The  presentation  was  missing  a  signiﬁcant  number  of  key  points.  
The  presentation  is unclear  and  does  not  provide  information  regarding  the  patient.  
 
2.  Summary  
Summarized  all  signiﬁcant  points  of  the  case.   
The  summary  included  the  majority  of  signiﬁcant  points  of  the  case.  
The  summary  missed  some  major  points  of  the  case.  
The  summary  missed  many  key  points.  
The  team  did  not  summarize  the  case  during  the  presentation.  
 
C.  Presentation  Delivery
 
EXCELLENT  5  points  
GOOD  4  points  
AVERAGE  3  points  
FAIR  2  points  
POOR  0  points  
JUDGE  SCORE  
1.  Voice   Pitch,  tempo,  volume,  quality  
The  competitor’s  voice  was  loud  enough  to  hear.  To  enhance  the  speech,  the  competitor  varied  the  rate  and  volume.  Appropriate  pausing  was  employed.  
The  competitor  spoke  loudly  and  clearly  enough  to  be  understood.  The  competitor  varied  the  rate  OR  volume  to  enhance  the  speech.  Pauses  were  attempted.  
The  competitor  could  be  heard  most  of  the  time.  The  competitor  attempted  to  use  some  variety  in  vocal  quality,  but  not  always  successfully.   
Judges  had  difﬁculty  hearing  /  understanding  much  of  the  speech  due  to  little  variety  in  rate  or  volume.  
The  competitor ’s  voice  is  too  low  or  monotone.   Judges  struggled  to  stay  focused  during  the  majority  of  presentation.

C.  Presentation  Delivery
 
EXCELLENT  5  points  
GOOD  4  points  
AVERAGE  3  points  
FAIR  2  points  
POOR  0  points  
JUDGE  SCORE  
2.  Stage  Presence  Poise,  posture,  eye  contact,  and  enthusiasm   
Movements  &  gestures  were  purposeful  and  enhanced  the  delivery  of  the  speech  and  did  not  distract.  Body  language  reﬂects  comfort  interacting  with  audience.      Facial  expressions  and  body  language  consistently  generated  a  strong  interest  and  enthusiasm  for  the  topic.  
The  competitor  maintained  adequate  posture  and  non-distracting  movement  during  the  speech.  Some  gestures  were  used.   Facial  expressions  and  body  language  sometimes  generated  an  interest  and  enthusiasm  for  the  topic.  
Stiff  or  unnatural  use  of  nonverbal  behaviors.  Body  language  reﬂects  some  discomfort  interacting  with  audience.  Limited  use  of  gestures  to  reinforce  verbal  message.   Facial  expressions  and  body  language  are  used  to  try  to  generate  enthusiasm  but  seem  somewhat  forced.   
The  competitor's  posture,  body  language,  and  facial  expressions  indicated  a  lack  of  enthusiasm  for  the  topic.  Movements  were  distracting.  
No  attempt  was  made  to  use  body  movement  or  gestures  to  enhance  the  message.  No  interest  or  enthusiasm  for  the  topic  came  through  in  presentation.  
 
3.  Diction*,  Pronunciation**  and  Grammar   *Deﬁnition  of  Diction  –  Choice  of  words,  especially  with  regard  to  correctness,  clearness,  and  effectiveness.  **Deﬁnition  of  Pronunciation  –  Act  or  manner  of  uttering  ofﬁcially.  
Delivery  emphasizes  and  enhances  message.  Clear  enunciation  and  pronunciation.  No  vocal  ﬁllers  (ex:  "ahs,"  "uh/ums,"  or  "you-knows”).  Tone  heightened  interest  and  complemented  the  verbal  message.  
Delivery  helps  to  enhance  message.  Clear  enunciation  and  pronunciation.  Minimal  vocal  ﬁllers  (ex:  "ahs,"  "uh/ums,"  or  "you-knows”).  Tone  complemented  the  verbal  message  
Delivery  adequate.  Enunciation  and  pronunciation  suitable.  Noticeable  verbal  ﬁllers  (ex:  "ahs,"  "uh/ums,"  or  "you-knows”)  present.  Tone  seemed  inconsistent  at  times.  
Delivery  quality  minimal.  Regular  verbal  ﬁllers  (ex:  "ahs,"  "uh/ums,"  or  "you-knows”)  present.  Delivery  problems  cause  disruption  to  message.  
Many  distracting  errors  in  pronunciation  and/or  articulation.  Monotone  or  inappropriate  variation  of  vocal  characteristics.  Inconsistent  with  verbal  message.  
 
C.  Presentation  Delivery
 
EXCELLENT  10  points  
GOOD  8  points  
AVERAGE  6  points  
FAIR  4  points  
POOR  0  points  
JUDGE  SCORE  
4.  Team  Participation   
This  is  an  excellent  example  of  shared  collaboration  in  the  presentation.  Both  team  members  spoke  and  carried  equal  parts  of  the  presentation.  
The  team  worked  well  together  with  the  presentation  almost  equally  balanced.  
The  team  worked  together  relatively  well.   The  presentation  could  have  been  more  balanced.   
The  team  did  not  work  together  as  effectively  as  needed  for  an  effective  presentation.  
One  team  member  dominated  the  presentation.  
 
Total  Points  (115)
